subject: Embeddia discovery — pilot criteria, compliance, and SDK alignment
messages:
From: kimberly_park <kimberly.park@redwoodinference.com>
To: Elena Torres <elena.torres@embeddia.ai>, Tom Becker <t.becker@embeddia.ai>
Cc: marcus_lin <marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com>, connor_obrien <connor.obrien@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, 15 Jun 2027 14:23:00 +0000
Subject: Embeddia discovery — pilot criteria, compliance, and SDK alignment

Hi Elena / Tom —

Thanks again for the intro call earlier. Quick recap while it’s fresh, and proposed next steps so we’re aligned on scope and owners. I’ve attached a one-page initial-pilot-scope.pdf.

Key pain points you called out
- Search relevance drops for domain-specific docs; current rerank runs in app and is expensive to maintain.
- Long tail of ad-hoc embeddings + storage duplication across services (cost + operational overhead).
- Need predictable latency for user-facing search (goal: median <200ms, p95 <500ms).

Current stack (from call)
- Backend: Node.js microservices on AWS EKS
- Vector store: Elasticsearch + custom embedding pipeline
- Auth & infra: Okta SSO, VPC-enabled, internal auditors require SOC2 evidence for production integrations

Success criteria for pilot (mutually agreed)
1) Integration: working SDK flow (Node or Python) that replaces current embedding pipeline for one vertical (KB articles).
2) Latency: median inference <200ms for 512-token context on Redwood Dedicated or Private; p95 acceptable within 500ms.
3) Cost: demonstrable token/unit cost lower than current monthly spend for the pilot traffic profile.
4) Security: SOC2 controls + audit logging available for the pilot.

Proposed PoC timeline (6 weeks, flexible)
- Week 0: NDA & project kickoff (this week)
- Week 1: Access & sample dataset + SDK smoke test (Node, Python)
- Week 2–3: Integration & embedding migration for KB vertical
- Week 4: Performance tuning & quantization options; validate latency/cost targets
- Week 5–6: Acceptance testing, handover docs, and final exec readout

Owners
- Redwood AE / owner: Kimberly Park (me) — contract / commercial lead
- Redwood SE: Marcus Lin — technical lead, SDK assist and perf tuning
- Redwood Integration Engineer: Connor O’Brien — handles deployment/runbook for Dedicated or Private option
- Embeddia PM: Elena Torres — pilot product owner

Immediate next steps (please confirm)
1) Elena: share the small sample dataset and any IP redaction needs (if you’d rather we use synthetic samples, say so).
2) Embeddia: confirm SOC2 evidence scope we’ll need for pilot (e.g., encryption, logging).
3) Redwood: Marcus will share a short SDK compatibility matrix and a Node quickstart repo by EOD tomorrow.
4) Schedule a 30-min technical sync with Marcus + Connor + your infra lead for Wed (US-PT/AU times noted in calendar invite).

Attachments: initial-pilot-scope.pdf (one-page scope)

Thanks — looking forward to getting this moving.

—
Kimberly Park
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
kimberly.park@redwoodinference.com | +1 (415) 555-0142

From: Elena Torres <elena.torres@embeddia.ai>
To: kimberly_park <kimberly.park@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Tom Becker <t.becker@embeddia.ai>
Date: Tue, 15 Jun 2027 18:05:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Embeddia discovery — pilot criteria, compliance, and SDK alignment

Thanks Kimberly — great summary. Confirming a few items from our side and adding constraints so we don’t miss them during scope.

Affirmations
- Pilot vertical: KB articles (first 100k docs) — agreed.
- Timeline: 6 weeks sounds reasonable, but procurement and legal need deliverables before we can go live (they want SOW + security questionnaire).

Constraints / must-haves
- Security: SOC2 Type II preferred; if Redwood cannot provide SOC2 evidence for the Dedicated offering we will require on-prem (air-gapped) proof-of-concept.
- Data residency: trial data must remain within us-east-1 for internal review.
- Performance gating: procurement requires p95 <600ms for at least 7 of 10 sample queries before approving paid pilot.

I’m attaching the security-questions.xlsx our security team prefilled with initial asks. We’ll add more detailed network/access controls after your SE reviews.

Next steps from Embeddia
- I’ll upload a redacted subset of KB docs by Thu EOD (we may need to strip PII).
- Tom will loop in procurement for SOW review — expect a redline cycle.

Appreciate Marcus sharing the SDK details — I’ll prioritize technical sync scheduling.

Best,
Elena
VP Product | Embeddia
elena.torres@embeddia.ai

From: marcus_lin <marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com>

Date: Wed, 16 Jun 2027 09:42:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Embeddia discovery — pilot criteria, compliance, and SDK alignment

Hi Elena — quick technical note and what I’ll deliver for the sync tomorrow.

1) SDK & language support- Node (official SDK)
- Python (official SDK)
- Go and Java are in beta — can provide examples but recommend Node/Python for pilot.

2) API compatibility & integration patterns- Two integration patterns we discussed:
  a) Client-side SDK for embedding: lightweight (Node/Python), calls Redwood hosted/dedicated endpoint; returns vector, then you upsert to Elasticsearch.
  b) Server-side direct API: Redwood-hosted embed + store in your ES via server batch jobs (recommended for simplicity).

3) Performance knobs- Recommended quantization profile: int8-fast for embed encoder; prefer fp16 on generator if using that path.
- KV cache warmup: pre-warm cache with sample queries to stabilize p95 during testing.

4) Security notes- We can provide SOC2 evidence for the Redwood Dedicated offering; for Private (on-prem) we provide the platform package and runbook for auditors.

Deliverables before the sync- sdk_compatibility_matrix.xlsx (attached) — maps endpoints, req/resp examples, and Node quickstart repo link.
- A 20-min demo script for the sync so we can validate latency on a small sample.

Quoted for context:
